messages:
Mina K: Hey team — booked the "Conference + Workshop" bundle for Berlin next month. Corporate card charged the conference fee ($820 EUR) but the vendor also charged a separate refundable equipment deposit (€120) which hit my personal card by mistake. Invoice comes in EUR, expense portal needs USD amounts. How do I submit the two charges so AP can reimburse me for the deposit and handle FX correctly?
Lexi (Finance): Hi Mina. Two parts: (1) corporate vs personal card split (you want refund for personal deposit), and (2) FX conversion. Please upload the vendor invoice and both card statements to Expensify. We prefer vendor invoice with EUR line items; if invoice shows only totals, include the booking confirmation screenshot that lists the deposit separately.
Mina K: Invoice PDF: https://vendor.example/invoices/CONF-44321.pdf — it lists "Conference Fee: 820.00 EUR" and "Deposit: 120.00 EUR". I attached a photo of my personal card statement showing the €120 charge: https://imgur.com/receipt-deposit.
Expense Bot: Reminder: attach receipt images and use the "Travel - Conference" category. Policy link: https://redwood.example/policies/expenses.
Evan (Manager): I confirm Mina attended the conference portion. Approve reimbursement of the refundable deposit charged to Mina's personal card. :white_check_mark:
Mina K: Great — do you want the EUR converted by me or will Finance convert to USD at the company rate? The portal asked me for exchange rate.
Lexi (Finance): Finance will perform FX conversion at the payment date using the corporate exchange table. For now submit the amounts in original currency and add a note: "Do not convert — use corporate FX at payment". Also add the card authorization / refund status if vendor issues a refund later.
Mina K: One more wrinkle — the vendor invoice shows VAT included for the conference fee (19%) but marks the deposit as "non-taxable". Can we reclaim VAT on the conference fee if it's an event?
Lexi (Finance): If the vendor provides VAT amount and their VAT registration number, we can reclaim input VAT for the business portion. Please ensure the invoice has the vendor VAT ID and the VAT line item. In this case the invoice lists VAT: 19% on 820 EUR and no VAT on deposit. Uploading that will let us code the conference line to TRAVEL-VAT and deposit to TRAVEL-NONRECLAIM.
Mina K: Uploaded both to Expensify: https://expensify.com/receipts/xyz987. Included vendor VAT ID and screenshot of my card.
Lexi (Finance): Received. Two operational items: (1) enter two separate expense lines in the portal: "Conference Fee — 820.00 EUR — TRAVEL-VAT" and "Equipment Deposit — 120.00 EUR — TRAVEL-NONRECLAIM"; (2) mark payment method: corporate card paid conference fee so no reimbursement for that; deposit reimbursed to Mina. We'll create AP entries accordingly.
Mina K: If vendor refunds the deposit later, do I need to submit anything?
Lexi (Finance): If vendor refunds the deposit to your personal card, we will offset future reimbursements or process a chargeback. Preferred process: ask vendor to refund to the same card and notify Finance with refund confirmation (transaction ID). If refunded after we process reimbursement, we'll request you to either return the amount or we will net it against expenses in the next payroll as a deduction (we'll confirm with you first).
Avery (CFO): Quick note — because conference fee > $750 and VAT reclaim is involved, I approve the VAT reclaim submission and the deposit reimbursement. Finance proceed and confirm FX rate used once payment processes.
Expense Bot: Expense queued (ref EXP-2026-00901). Pending AP posting and FX conversion.
Mina K: Thanks all, filing this now. I'll follow up if vendor issues refund.
Lexi (Finance): Thanks Mina. We'll email confirmation when AP posts and when payment is scheduled. :email:
